rubric_items.reason: All four ticket acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-4; the display change and job frequency are listed under Out of scope with reasons.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable; REQ-6 bundles four staff actions and does not say what state a rescheduled Stale appointment returns to.
Every known item cites the ticket, the context pack or an IDE answer (a-01..a-05); the cited answers say what the artifact claims.
Both baseline clashes (only Scheduled can change; actor always staff) were asked, answered and recorded as mismatches with glossary cites.
Questions were real gaps (window, mechanism, mutability, actor, glossary) with concrete options; none remain open or blocking.
Readable; status names switch between the data-model codes (SCHEDULED, NO_SHOW) and glossary terms (Scheduled, No-show) in one statement.

findings.text: REQ-6 is compound: four separate transitions (complete, no-show, cancel, reschedule) in one REQ. It also does not say what state a rescheduled Stale appointment ends in (Scheduled again?), so a tester cannot check that outcome.

cites.quote: Staff can still mark a Stale appointment Completed or No-show, cancel it or reschedule it (`complete, no-show, cancel, reschedule`).
answer: Yes: complete, no-show, cancel, reschedule (proposed default)

findings.suggested_fix: Split REQ-6 into one REQ per transition. For the reschedule one, state the resulting status (presumably Scheduled) as assumed, based on A-03.

findings.text: The Out-of-scope reason says the ticket does not ask for a display change. But the ticket's stated goal is that a Stale appointment no longer looks like an upcoming Scheduled one, which is about how it is shown.

cites.quote: the ticket does not ask for a display change
looking like an upcoming Scheduled appointment

findings.suggested_fix: Reword the reason: the status change alone satisfies the goal, and any list, filter or tile change is deferred to design.

findings.text: REQ-1 mixes the database codes (SCHEDULED, NO_SHOW) with the glossary term Stale. Other REQs use the glossary forms Scheduled and No-show.

cites.quote: alongside SCHEDULED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED and NO_SHOW

findings.suggested_fix: Use the glossary terms Scheduled, Completed, Cancelled and No-show in requirement statements.

cites.quote: COMPLETED, CANCELLED or NO_SHOW; a cancellation reason exists exactly when CANCELLED.
`appointment_event` records every change with time and actor.
a Scheduled appointment is rescheduled, cancelled with a reason, or marked Completed or No-show.
